chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: Learn to read music, and singers who never credit his arrangements
summary: He tells musicians to read since there is no place for ear pianists like Erroll Garner, and complains that Alberta Hunter, Della Reese and Ruby Dee never mention him.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: See, all those guys I had under me, see, they came through me in the theatre, and the musicians the same way -- I used to tell the musicians, hey, learn to read music, learn to read music -- because they have no place for an ear piano player now, what's the boy that just died?
Piano player?
Yeah.
Oh, Errol Garner.
Errol Garner, see. Errol Garner to me was the only piano player that didn't read that was still playing, see.
Right.
And he played them "off" chords. I listened to him the other day, and I said well, he lasted a long while.
Sure did.
What's the girl down The Cookery now?
Singer?
Yeah.
Oh ...
Eight-five years old. See, I wrote some of her numbers. She used to come to the house and I used to write for her, and oh, what's her name.
Let me stop the tape while I think of her name.
The name that keeps escaping us was who?
Her name was Alberta Hunter.
Right, and what were you saying about her?
And she used to come to the house and I used to -- you know, she used to sing, and I used to put it down and orchestrate it for her and she never mentions me.
Della Reese. Remember Della Reese?
Yes sir.
Well, she's another girl that I used to do her copying. Mostly used to do her arranging, see?
Uh huh. You know, that's unfortunate, but I'm glad we're mentioning it now.
You know, nearly every singer -- Ruby Dee, do you remember her?
: Oh sure.
All right. She was -- I was coaching her singing, and she left me and went somewhere, and all of a sudden, I hear Ruby Dee!
